response.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT o.mktnote AS mktnote, f.feerate - f.rebrate AS net FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = f.orderslink), overall AS (SELECT AVG(net) AS a FROM m), g AS (SELECT mktnote, AVG(net) AS a FROM m GROUP BY mktnote) SELECT AVG(g.a) AS mean_pair_avg_net_fee_rate, AVG(g.a - overall.a) AS mean_excess_over_overall FROM g CROSS JOIN overall WHERE g.a > overall.a

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique per order, so the join does not duplicate fee rows. The overall average is taken over all matched fee rows (fee-row weighted), not over the pair averages.
Rows with NULL mktnote form one group. An empty-string mktnote is treated as its own distinct pair, not as missing.
A fee row with a NULL feerate or NULL rebrate has a NULL net rate and is skipped in the averages. Skipped rows are not treated as a zero rebate.
If no pair exceeds the overall average, or the overall average is NULL, the query returns one row of NULLs.
